explanation.headline: Bet 33% was the top play; checking loses 2.33 bb against Villain's range.

paragraphs: You held 6♦ 7♦ in the big blind, against Villain, a LAG player, on the button. Pre-flop, Villain opened to 2.5 bb and you called.
The flop came 3♠ K♣ 3♣: you checked and Villain checked. The turn was the T♦: you checked, Villain bet 4 bb and you called. The river was the 8♠. It was your turn to act with 13 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Check (EV 0.55 bb). The top play was Bet 33% (EV 2.88 bb), so your choice gives up 2.33 bb against Villain's range. Verdict: Mistake.
Your equity against Villain's whole range is 5.4%.

Bet 33%: Villain folds 42% of the time, more than the 25.7% a bet this size needs to profit on folds alone (4.5 bb / (13 bb + 4.5 bb)), so folds alone pay for it, even when every hand that continues beats you. On top of that, you have 1.4% equity against the hands that continue.
The largest parts of the range are Air (35.3% of it; your equity 15%) and Weak made hand (24.7% of it; your equity 0%).
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a LAG player. Loose-aggressive: wide ranges, frequent pressure, more bluffs.
Villain's range narrowed with each action: Pre-flop: opens to 2.5 bb; Flop: checks; Turn: bets 4 bb (80% pot).
The range in the Range tab is the range this puzzle was graded on.
